scope_note: Adds to pass 1 (ktm-rider-feedback.json). Findings are short paraphrases of the article text that WebFetch returned. Newest first; undated items are placed by best evidence and flagged. Forum entries are individual experience, not tests. No source in this pass gave part numbers.

feedback.product: Feature unlock for map switching, traction control, launch assist and Quickshift
feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: Comparison of the stock 2026 MC450F with the KTM 450 SX-F and Husqvarna FC450. No aftermarket parts were fitted.
feedback.observed: These features are locked on the GasGas and cost about $200 to unlock. Lawson attributes a slightly harsher feel to the GasGas's forged triple clamps (KTM and Husqvarna use machined clamps). He also says the stock Maxxis tires may not match the Dunlops, though the difference doesn't last long. This is the only 2026 GasGas written test found, and it tested no aftermarket parts.
feedback.measured: 229 lb without fuel (author's scale; the same for all three bikes). MSRP: MC450F $10,849, KTM 450 SX-F $11,649, FC450 FE $13,799.

feedback.brand: WP (Pro Components / A-Kit), tuned by REP Suspension (Mark Johnson)
feedback.product: WP Pro Components fork and shock
feedback.author: Tokarski710 (byline; first-person tester not named)
feedback.conditions: Fox Raceway, one full day; 180 lb ex-pro rider; pump gas; 105 mm sag (not changed). Built by Luc Santos (Factory Motocross Vacations).
feedback.observed: Good small-to-medium bump absorption and a level, balanced feel. The shock damping ramped up a bit quickly from mid to end stroke, and the fork felt soft from mid to end stroke. The rider changed damping front and rear and ended with a good balance.
feedback.other_mods: Vortex/TD ECU, FMF 4.1 with 250F-spec Megabomb header, KTM PowerParts split clamps, Nacstar/DID STX wheels, Raptor Ti pegs, Hinson clutch cover, Moto-Seat cover, Renthal bars/grips/sprockets (rear one tooth down), Dunlop MX34

feedback.product: Vortex ECU with TD map
feedback.author: Tokarski710 (byline)
feedback.conditions: As p2-002; pump gas
feedback.observed: Stronger low-rpm power, crisper throttle, better rpm recovery in ruts and a smoother over-rev. The rider found no real downside. The FMF 4.1 system (250F-spec Megabomb header) was also credited for the engine gains but got no separate comments. The article credits the tuning to 'Jamie Ellis' in one place and to Twisted Development in another.
feedback.other_mods: See p2-002

feedback.product: Titanium footpegs
feedback.author: Tokarski710 (byline)
feedback.observed: Noticeably more grip than stock; the feet slipped less. No negatives stated.
feedback.other_mods: See p2-002

feedback.product: Nacstar wheelset with DID STX rims
feedback.author: Tokarski710 (byline)
feedback.conditions: As p2-002; no back-to-back test against the stock wheels
feedback.observed: Felt similar to stock on track; the rider valued them for durability. Compare MXA's 2022 build, where NacStar wheels had no problems on race day (pass 1 build).
feedback.other_mods: See p2-002

feedback.product: Moto-Seat seat cover; Renthal half-waffle grips (cut down from full-waffle)
feedback.author: Tokarski710 (byline)
feedback.observed: The seat cover kept the rider forward when driving out of corners. The grips were more comfortable than his usual Kevlar grips without losing control.
feedback.other_mods: See p2-002

feedback.brand: Vortex (Twisted Development or XPR maps); TZR, TD and XPR stock-ECU reflash; KTM Connectivity Unit
feedback.product: Vortex ECU vs stock-ECU remap vs CUO on 2023+ 350 SX-F / FC350
feedback.publication: Vital MX forum (threads 'Vortex ECU on 23+ KTM 350SXF' and '2024 Ktm 350 sxf stock remap vs vortex ecu')
feedback.author: dizzy8085, GoggleFiend904, FGR01, bvm111, Chris_Buehler, stumpy823, Langhammx, Smith246, crmx105, Ob917, cwtoyota, skyrebel88, yzrider53, Rider 5280, CR23, Mr. Plump and others
feedback.conditions: Individual owners, March 2025 to January 2026. Fuels range from pump gas to 93 octane. FGR01 rides at about 4,200 ft; bvm111 weighs 215 lb and runs a 51T rear sprocket.
feedback.observed: Individual experiences. Most owners say the Vortex cured decel popping and flame-outs and gave more bottom end and top pull (dizzy8085, Chris_Buehler, Langhammx, bvm111). stumpy823 (TD, 2024 350) called it the best money he has spent. Dissent: GoggleFiend904 seldom used the maps or features after a few weeks and felt it wasn't worth the cost. FGR01 (2025 FC350, TD) says the quickshifter cuts ignition too hard and the elevation maps felt soft. bvm111 calls the Vortex a clear upgrade but not essential on the new generation. Smith246 says his 2025 350 runs clean stock. Ob917 warns that flame-outs may point to a fault the Vortex won't fix. On the CUO: crmx105 and Smith246 said it did little for engine braking. On stock-ECU remaps: skyrebel88 and yzrider53 were happy with a remap (TD for yzrider53). Mr. Plump says TZR told him it cannot remap 2023+ ECUs. CR23 found a TD Vortex on his 2018-19 350 a letdown.
feedback.measured: User-reported costs: about $1,100 for a new TD Vortex, $600 for a used TD unit without TC/QS, and $110 for a TZR reflash on a 2022 350 (estimated 10% gain, self-reported). The second thread's opener cites about $800 extra for a Vortex over a stock remap.
feedback.other_mods: Varies (Akrapovic slip-on, HGS full system, vented airbox)

feedback.product: Rekluse auto clutch (exact model not named)
feedback.author: Gardner Tarlow (posted by Kris Keefer)
feedback.conditions: About 30 hours: high and low desert, single track, SoCal MX tracks, local GPs. Senior vet, open-novice speed, 5'10" and 185 lb; rides 2-3 times a week. Installed by a friend following Rekluse's online instructions.
feedback.observed: No more stalling, even in gear at a stop. Smoother low-speed response with no cough or stall in slow technical terrain, less need to feather the clutch in corners, more controlled descents without the rear kicking, and it felt like better hookup on the MX track. The lever can still be popped to clear obstacles. Downsides: blipping the throttle in gear at idle can launch the bike (start and stop with the lever pulled in); using the lever like a standard clutch can overheat it; the bike rolls back on a hill with the engine off (the left-hand rear brake is a workaround). The tester also found the stock spring fork a bit soft for faster MX. This is the 2023+ clutch-generation test that pass 1 lacked.
feedback.other_mods: None stated; a Vortex was considered but not fitted

feedback.product: Handmade cone pipe + full carbon silencer (stamped pipe and alloy silencer with carbon end cap also offered)
feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: Several test riders, including faster riders. Glen Helen's Mount Saint Helens hill is the reference point.
feedback.observed: More midrange and top end with no change to the bottom end: a stronger midrange surge and less drop-off at over-rev, so gears can be held longer. The carbon silencer stays cooler, and testers liked the sound and the craftsmanship. Downsides: the head pipe sits farther out than stock, so it is more exposed to damage; the silencer was fiddly to install until the mounts were aligned; the bare finish rusts without care; the mount kit was missing hardware and came without instructions (the importer, Motoman Distributing, supplied the bolts).
feedback.measured: No dyno figures. Prices: cone pipe $329, stamped pipe $249, full carbon silencer $359, alloy silencer with carbon end cap $209.

feedback.product: Map switch (unlocks map 2, Quick Shift, TC); Nihilo radiator cap removal tool
feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: MXA race test of the stock bike
feedback.observed: Without the switch the bike is stuck in the mellow map 1. The Nihilo tool is recommended because the new plastic radiator cap is hard to fit and remove and seems less durable than the older 1.8 cap. On the stock bike, testers found the BrakTec front brake much improved over 2023 but still less precise than Brembo; a recall covers 2022-2025 GasGas front brakes. The stock Neken bar's riser is 12 mm taller than KTM's.
feedback.measured: Map switch just under $200. The text gives 14/52 gearing, but a photo caption says 51T is stock (conflict).

feedback.brand: KTM PowerParts / Nihilo Concepts / Ride Engineering / Twin Air
feedback.product: PowerParts map switch; CUO; Nihilo radiator cap tool; Nihilo or Ride Engineering start/stop button relocation; Twin Air airbox wash covers; lower-bend handlebar (brand not named)
feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: MXA race test of the stock bike
feedback.observed: Testers say the map switch is worth buying because it unlocks map 2, launch control, TC and Quickshift; the KTM 350 SX-F and FC350 include it. The CUO is fun but not necessary: testers use only engine-braking adjustment and a map tool that increases the acceleration rate. They suggest a lower-bend bar because the stock bars sit 12 mm taller than KTM's. Some remove the GasGas frame guards because they push the feet out. The latest WP shock collar is easier to use and more durable.
feedback.measured: Map switch $180; CUO $249.99; LitPro $69.99 per year

feedback.product: Dunlop MX33F front tire in place of the stock AT81F; rear sprocket changes from stock 14/48 to 14/49 (fast terrain) or 14/50-52 (general riding)
feedback.author: Trevor Hunter
feedback.date: 2025 (not printed; images uploaded April 2025; page modified 2025-12-13)
feedback.conditions: About 35 hours: SoCal hare and hounds, desert at 70-80 mph, rocks and extreme enduro. Several testers of mixed size and skill. 91 pump gas at 50:1.
feedback.observed: The MX33F front gave better bump absorption and traction than the AT81F. The author recommends a better rear tire than the AT81 (no model named) and lower gearing for most riding. Testers shortened the shock internally by 1-3 mm and some ran the fork flush or below flush in the clamps, because the new spring fork is 10 mm shorter and makes the front feel low. The author tried unnamed ECUs and tuning options. Stock BrakTec brakes are firmer than Brembo but less linear and fade sooner.
feedback.measured: Rear sag went from 107-108 mm to 100-105 mm after the shock change. Some owners recalibrate the TPS every 15-20 hours. MSRP $10,749.
feedback.other_mods: Motorex and Maxima injector premix at 50:1 (no issues)

feedback.product: Dal Soggio Sphere FSR-48 spring forks; Ohlins RXF 48S; WP 6500 cartridge; KYB coil-spring kits
feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: MXA race test; testers have raced all of these forks
feedback.observed: MXA says coil forks in general give better hand comfort, follow the ground better and save setup time, and testers 'loved' the KYB kits. But a well set-up stock XACT air fork does some things the kits can't, so the upgrade may not be necessary. MXA also says an aftermarket linkage (brand not named) will not fit the 2025 because of its smaller bolts. Compare pass-1 ktm-fb-006: the Ride Engineering linkage fits 2024.5-2025.5 but not 2023-2024. The KTM vented airbox cover improves throttle response, and one extra rear sprocket tooth adds low-end grunt for riders who ride low in the rpm range.
feedback.measured: Aftermarket forks about $2,000-$7,000. Stock baseline: 10.7 bar (155 psi), 105 mm sag. CUO $249.99, retrofittable to 2023-2025.

feedback.brand: Raptor / Mitigator / Motoes / Flo Motorsports / Fastway / Carapaks
feedback.product: Lowered and offset footpegs for the 2023+ KTM peg mount
feedback.publication: Vital MX forum ('23/24 KTM lowered footpeg options?')
feedback.author: Ray Knight, Bruce372, Langhammx, Richy (Mitigator), GoggleFiend904, mx-doctor, masonraines, nathan4765, Derpin' DJ
feedback.conditions: Individual owners, November 2023 to April 2024. Ray Knight is 6'6"; masonraines is 6'3".
feedback.observed: Individual experiences. Bruce372 fitted Raptor pegs 5 mm down and 10 mm back (bought from the UK): easier shifting with size 10-11 boots, a more open feel, and better shock performance from the weight shift. Langhammx agreed. Richy, posting for the maker Mitigator, said their earlier-generation pegs sat lower and farther back than advertised. masonraines found his Flo pegs sat at stock height on a 2023 350 SX-F and went back to stock. Ray Knight dislikes spiked pegs because they wear boot soles, prefers screw-pin pegs, and noted the 2023+ pegs use a new mount. When the thread started, Fastway offered only rear offset at stock height and Flo had no lowered peg for the new chassis. Riders felt rearward offset mattered more than drop on this chassis.
feedback.measured: Motoes stainless -10 mm/-10 mm about $109 (user-quoted price; no riding report)

feedback.brand: Rekluse / throttle cam brand not named
feedback.product: Rekluse CX clutch (the final thoughts call it a 'Core auto', which is inconsistent) + slower-turning throttle cam
feedback.author: Ron Lawson (tester Jeff Slavens)
feedback.conditions: Colorado trails at 6,300-12,000 ft: rocky, rooty, technical, plus whoops and faster sections. One tank stock, then modified. Slavens remapped ECU (details not given).
feedback.observed: The clutch and slower throttle cam made the very strong stock engine more manageable. The stock XC was harsh and unforgiving in rocks and roots because of its stiffer chassis, swingarm and valving. Slavens made suspension his top priority, and only with the clutch and suspension done did he call it a 'stellar' Colorado off-roader. He would still pick the XC-W (out of scope) for comfort.
feedback.measured: Altitude: over 20% less compression at 6,300 ft than at sea level (as stated). Stock XC range about 45 miles; Acerbis 3.2 gal tank fitted.
feedback.other_mods: FSW-revalved WP AER fork and XACT shock, later Slavens Mule Raven fork and MX-Tech National shock; Molecule skid plate; Bullet Proof radiator guards; Fastway Evo 4 low-boy pegs; Tubliss; Steahly flywheel weight (planned, not fitted)

feedback.product: AIM Taipan ECU with custom maps vs Vortex ECU
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen, dry and edgy; hard-pack, choppy and rutted. Riders 175-200 lb. Settings applied after at least an 8-hour break-in.
feedback.observed: Taipan: per-gear mapping, a longer-pulling second gear, smoother low end, more mid-to-top, better exit traction and gentler response in ruts; much better than stock overall. Vortex: better rear traction and a step up on stock, but Keefer had not yet found the pull length the AIM gave him. This disagrees with his 2024 article (pass-1 ktm-fb-015), which rated the Taipan below the Vortex because fewer tuners support it and it is harder to get.
feedback.other_mods: FMF system (insert in), Ride Engineering 23.5mm clamps, WP 6500 kit / REP-AEO valving, Pro Component shock

feedback.product: REP/AEO valving and springs (fork and shock), plus WP Pro Component shock
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested with REP's Mark at Glen Helen; riders 175-200 lb
feedback.observed: No pitching off-throttle, more comfort on small chop near the top of the stroke, and good end-stroke damping. Keefer says it brought back the 2022 chassis's cornering feel. Swingarm pivot torque reduced to 95 Nm helped settle the rear.
feedback.measured: Stock baseline: fork height 5 mm, 10.9 bar, C 15 out, R 16 out; shock sag 106 mm, LSC 12 out, HSC 1.25 out, R 16 out. Gearing 13/51; chain slack 68-70 mm.
feedback.other_mods: See p2-016

feedback.product: Factory 4.1 RCT titanium slip-on with carbon end cap (stock header kept)
feedback.author: Donn Maeda (author bio; no separate byline)
feedback.conditions: Cahuilla Creek, about 3,500 ft (the author thinks gains may be bigger lower down). Tested with the spark arrestor in and out, both maps, and TC on and off. A Glen Helen race follow-up was planned.
feedback.observed: Arrestor out: louder, revs more freely, more top-end pull. Arrestor in: more low-end torque and smoother, but it revved less per gear, the author found no power gain, and he says the arrestor is only for compliance. Five-minute install reusing the stock grommets; no longer than stock, lighter, and sound stays reasonable. Downsides: louder; the arrestor comes out only by removing a circlip inside the end cap.
feedback.measured: $799.99. No dyno or sound figures.
feedback.other_mods: None

feedback.product: RS-12 titanium full system with carbon end cap

bike.model: 250 SX-F (article title; the fetched summary also says dyno results looked good on a 350)

feedback.author: Not stated
feedback.conditions: Baseline on the stock exhaust at Perris Raceway, swapped in the pits, then ridden at Glen Helen and Cahuilla Creek by several test riders. No mapping or engine work.
feedback.observed: Stronger low-end response and midrange than stock, fills the stock flat spot before the midrange, and extends over-rev. Good welds and finish; fits well; comes with a spring puller. The author calls it the biggest gain he has felt from an aftermarket four-stroke exhaust in years. No negatives stated. In Swapmoto's 2024 350 SX-F Dream Build, builder Jamie Ellis (Twisted Development) calls the RS-12 the best aftermarket exhaust for the 250s and 350s (builder opinion, not a test).
feedback.measured: $1,299. The article mentions dyno testing but gives no figures.
feedback.other_mods: None on the test bike

feedback.brand: KTM OEM (Dirt Star rims) vs DID STX rims with Bulldog spokes; Fasst Co spoke torque wrench
feedback.product: Stock spoke wheels: seating and loosening; aftermarket rebuilds
feedback.author: adams189, Nitrofunnycar, racinstation, MKMX, FGR01, Hammer 663s, Darrin Willis, Gravel and others
feedback.conditions: Individual owners. Only the original poster has a 2023 model.
feedback.observed: Individual experiences. Spokes loosening over the first rides is widely reported and usually treated as normal seating. Owners torque spokes periodically (Fasst wrench mentioned several times); the spoke next to the rim lock loosens first. racinstation thinks the 2022-23 Austrian wheels need more attention than before. FGR01 says the stock Dirt Star rims on Husky and KTM FE wheels are weaker and flat-spot more easily; after broken rear nipples he rebuilt with DID STX rims and Bulldog spokes and has had no further trouble. Gravel warns that seating spokes with a hammer can break a hub. This matches MXA's note on the KTM factory wheels (pass-1 ktm-fb-010).
feedback.measured: FGR01 recommends 5.5 Nm spoke torque instead of KTM's 6 Nm to avoid broken nipples (user advice)

feedback.product: TD exhaust flange
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Track flange comparison; Keefer tried several sizes and shapes. Tested on the stock muffler and with a full FMF system. No remap.
feedback.observed: Better response from mid-corner to exit, more pull out of corners and better third-gear lugging. Revs pick up faster, which he says makes the bike feel lighter over bumps. Works with stock and aftermarket exhausts and installs in minutes. No negatives stated. This matches his 2022 FC450 verdict (pass-1 ktm-fb-037).
feedback.measured: Price given as $200 in one place and $250 in another (inconsistent)
feedback.other_mods: Stock muffler or FMF full system

feedback.product: Hybrid AER fork (right leg cartridge swapped for one that takes a coil spring) + shock revalve with 4.8 N/mm spring; Scotts steering damper; SRT fork bleeders
feedback.author: Dirt Bike Staff (rider Ryan Koch, per photo caption)
feedback.conditions: Trail only: rocks, braking bumps, chop, whoops, hill climbs and technical trail. Rider 185+ lb with gear. 91 octane.
feedback.observed: The stock XACT air fork needed 140+ psi, which made it harsh at first and caused ramping. The hybrid ran at 50-60 psi and gave a plush initial stroke, controlled mid-stroke and strong bottoming resistance. The shock was balanced, resisted kicking, and didn't wallow at speed. The steering damper added stability. No downsides stated.
feedback.measured: Fork $875; shock revalve and spring $350. Spring 4.8 N/m as printed (likely N/mm), three rates stiffer than stock, for 190-210 lb total.
feedback.other_mods: See the TX300 build

feedback.product: Thunder Products Quad Flow dual torque wings (throttle body); Dicks Racing Hi-Torque head mod; Dicks Racing remap of the stock ECU (fuel, timing, oil ratio)
feedback.author: Dirt Bike Staff
feedback.observed: Torque wings: more torque, especially below half throttle; fitting means cutting grooves in the throttle body, so the editors suggest having Dicks Racing do it. Head: meatier bottom end immediately, no detonation, and ran cool under heavy load. Remap: better delivery and reliability, no figures. The Scalvini pipe and silencer got no separate comments.
feedback.measured: Wings $295 installed; head $195; remap $375; Scalvini exhaust $379. No dyno figures.
feedback.other_mods: See the TX300 build

feedback.product: TD exhaust flange (shaped to the aluminum exhaust port)
feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: Stock exhaust, no mapping changes. Vet riders and riders who liked the stock low end.
feedback.observed: Every tester felt more power off idle and quicker revving, with sharper low-to-mid response that carried into the midrange and top. Simple two-bolt install, and the gasket can often be reused. Riders happy with stock power saw the gain but didn't think it was worth the price. This agrees with Keefer (p2-021, pass-1 ktm-fb-037).
feedback.measured: $249.95. No dyno.
feedback.other_mods: None

feedback.product: One-piece titanium footpegs
feedback.author: Not stated (tester Matthew Horton)
feedback.conditions: Project bike compared against a 2020.5 450 SX-F Factory Edition; track not named. Tester is a regular FE rider.
feedback.observed: The author calls them the trickest aftermarket pegs he has tried, while admitting they weren't strictly necessary. No functional negatives stated.
feedback.measured: $799.99; half an inch wider than stock; 5.3 oz lighter than the stock cast titanium pegs
feedback.other_mods: See the Swapmoto Factory Edition Killer build

feedback.product: TorqDrive clutch pack (12 friction / 12 steel vs 8/8 stock)
feedback.author: Not stated (tester Matthew Horton)
feedback.conditions: As p2-025. The stock clutch was described as slipping under acceleration.
feedback.observed: Gave 'instant torque and throttle response' and cured the stock slipping. No negatives stated. This is the older clutch generation; the 2023+ test is p2-008.
feedback.other_mods: See the Swapmoto Factory Edition Killer build

feedback.product: WP spring conversion kit for the XACT 48 fork (single-sided coil spring) + REP fork and shock revalve
feedback.author: Not stated (tester Matthew Horton)
feedback.observed: Comfortable and predictable front end: handled braking chop well, resisted diving mid-corner, and no front-to-rear seesaw. The author generally dislikes single-function forks but says this one 'feels amazing'. This agrees with the positive single-spring reports but contrasts with the forum doubts about single-sided imbalance (pass-1 ktm-fb-051, ktm-fb-052).
feedback.measured: About $2,500 combined for the TD engine package and suspension rebuild (intro figure)
feedback.other_mods: See the Swapmoto Factory Edition Killer build

feedback.product: FCP billet aluminum engine mounts; KTM PowerParts Factory split triple clamp (reversible stem, 20/22 mm offset)
feedback.author: Not stated (tester Matthew Horton)
feedback.observed: FCP mounts: more torsional flex, a plusher feel over chop and better lean control in rutted corners, which agrees with Swapmoto's 2023 350 SX-F FCP test (pass-1 ktm-fb-028). Clamps: the split design reduces fork-tube binding and the offset is adjustable; the author was enthusiastic. Compare MXA, who saw no performance gain from WP split clamps (pass-1 ktm-fb-009).
feedback.other_mods: See the Swapmoto Factory Edition Killer build

feedback.product: Stage 1 engine package (CNC head porting and decking, valve seat work, ECU reprogram with EFI maps)
feedback.author: Not stated (tester Matthew Horton)
feedback.observed: Pulled harder and sooner than the tester expected, so he had to change his shift and acceleration points; strong low, mid and top. The author judged the project bike better than the 2020.5 FE (editorial judgment, not measured).
feedback.measured: $850 (footer price). No dyno.
feedback.other_mods: FMF Factory 4.1 Megabomb (claimed gains, no observation)
